# Psalm 88 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-song. A-psalm of-the-sons-of Korah. To-the-choirmaster. On Mahalath-Leannoth. A-maskil of-Heman the-Ezrahite.

**2** O-YHWH God-of my-salvation, by-day I-cry-out, in-the-night before-you.

**3** Let-come before-you my-prayer; incline your-ear to-my-cry.

**4** For is-full of-troubles my-soul, and-my-life to-Sheol has-drawn-near.

**5** I-am-counted with-those-going-down to-the-pit; I-have-become like-a-man without strength.

**6** Among the-dead set-free, like the-slain lying-in the-grave, whom not you-remember again, and-they from-your-hand are-cut-off.

**7** You-have-put-me in-pit lowest, in-dark-places, in-the-depths.

**8** Upon-me rests your-wrath, and-with-all your-breakers you-have-afflicted. Selah.

**9** You-have-removed my-acquaintances from-me; you-have-made-me an-abomination to-them; shut-in and-not I-can-go-out.

**10** My-eye has-grown-dim from-affliction; I-call-on-you O-YHWH every day; I-spread-out to-you my-hands.

**11** To-the-dead will-you-do wonders? Or-will the-shades rise to-praise-you? Selah.

**12** Will-be-declared in-the-grave your-steadfast-love? Your-faithfulness in-Abaddon?

**13** Will-be-known in-the-darkness your-wonder? And-your-righteousness in-land-of forgetfulness?

**14** And-I to-you O-YHWH I-cry-out, and-in-the-morning my-prayer meets-you.

**15** Why O-YHWH do-you-reject my-soul? Why do-you-hide your-face from-me?

**16** Afflicted I-am and-dying from-youth; I-bear your-terrors, I-am-numb.

**17** Over-me have-passed your-burning-wrath; your-terrors have-destroyed-me.

**18** They-surround-me like-water all the-day; they-close-in upon-me together.

**19** You-have-removed from-me lover and-friend; my-acquaintances — darkness.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **88:6**: 'Set-free among the dead' (bachofshy bammetim) — possibly 'released' to the realm of the dead; ironic 'freedom.'

- **88:11-13**: Five rhetorical questions — all expecting 'no' — pressing God: if the psalmist dies, there will be no praise from Sheol.

- **88:19**: Ends on 'darkness' (machshakh) — the only psalm that concludes without any note of hope or resolution.

— EMET
